explain.say: A vending machine's brain is a simple state machine: it is always in one state, like waiting or taking money, and each event moves it to the next state.

faq.a: A state machine is a system that is always in one of a few states and moves between them when events happen. A vending machine goes from waiting, to taking money, to vending, to giving change, and back.
asks: What is a finite state machine?

faq.q: How does a vending machine know a coin is real?
faq.a: Coins pass sensors that check their size, thickness and weight, and an electromagnetic coil tests the metal they are made of. Coins that don't match are sent to the return slot.
asks: How does a coin slot detect fake coins?

faq.q: How does a vending machine know the snack dropped?
faq.a: Many have infrared light beams across the space below the shelves. A falling item breaks the beams; if nothing does, the machine turns the spiral again or gives a refund.
asks: What if my snack gets stuck?

faq.q: How does a vending machine give the right change?
faq.a: It subtracts the price from your credit and pays out the difference from the coins stored in its change tubes.
asks: How does a vending machine work out change?

faq.q: Why does a vending machine reject my coin sometimes?
faq.a: If a coin is worn, bent or dirty, its measurements may fall outside the accepted range. Trying again, or using another coin, often works.
asks: Why does the machine keep spitting out my coin?

facts: One of the earliest known coin-operated machines, described by Hero of Alexandria in the first century, dispensed holy water.
Many vending machines use infrared beams to confirm that a product has actually dropped.

quiz.say: You press a code but have not paid enough. What does the state machine do?

options.show: Waits for more money and shows the price
options.say: Waits for more money and shows the price

options.show: Keeps your money and switches off
options.say: Keeps your money and switches off

quiz.why: It checks the credit first, so it stays in the paying state and asks for the rest.

wrong.1: It checks credit before vending, so nothing drops.
wrong.2: It keeps your credit and simply waits for more money.
